title: Undirected graphical models and sparse precision estimation

items.title: Finite undirected graphs, Markov properties, and clique factorization
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, with $E$ a set of unordered two-element subsets of $V$. A clique is a nonempty subset $C\subseteq V$ whose distinct vertices are adjacent. Let $(X_i)_{i\in V}$ be random elements on a common probability space, and for $U\subseteq V$ put $\mathcal F_U=\sigma(X_i:i\in U)$, with $\mathcal F_\emptyset=\{\emptyset,\Omega\}$. A path is a finite sequence of distinct vertices with adjacent consecutive vertices; $C$ separates $A$ from $B$ if every path from $A$ to $B$ meets $C$. The pairwise Markov property is $\mathcal F_{\{i\}}\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal F_{\{j\}}\mid\mathcal F_{V\setminus\{i,j\}}$ whenever $i\ne j$ and $\{i,j\}\notin E$. The global Markov property is $\mathcal F_A\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal F_B\mid\mathcal F_C$ whenever $A,B,C\subseteq V$ are pairwise disjoint and $C$ separates $A$ from $B$. If each $X_i$ takes values in a finite nonempty state space $\mathcal X_i$, a finite-state clique-factorized mass function on $G$ is $p(x)=Z^{-1}\prod_{C\in\mathcal C}\psi_C(x_C)$, where $\mathcal C$ is a finite collection of nonempty cliques, $\psi_C:\prod_{i\in C}\mathcal X_i\to(0,\infty)$, and $Z=\sum_{x\in\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal X_i}\prod_{C\in\mathcal C}\psi_C(x_C)$. The product state space and sum are finite, and every potential is positive and finite, so $0<Z<\infty$ and $p$ is a probability mass function. No equivalence between the clique-factorized class and either Markov property is asserted here.

items.title: Gaussian sparse-precision objective with the all-entry penalty
items.statement: For $N,p\ge1$ and data $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^p$, put $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^N x_r$ and $S=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^N(x_r-\bar x)(x_r-\bar x)^T$. For any symmetric positive-semidefinite $S$ and any $\Theta\in\mathbb S_{++}^p$, set $\ell_S(\Theta)=\log\det\Theta-\operatorname{tr}(S\Theta)$, where $\mathbb S_{++}^p$ is the cone of symmetric positive-definite $p\times p$ matrices. Define $\|\Theta\|_1=\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^p|\Theta_{ij}|$, including diagonal entries, and for $\lambda>0$ define $F_{S,\lambda}(\Theta)=\ell_S(\Theta)-\lambda\|\Theta\|_1$. The off-diagonal-only convention $F^{\mathrm{off}}_{S,\lambda}(\Theta)=\ell_S(\Theta)-\lambda\sum_{i\ne j}|\Theta_{ij}|$ is a separate objective.

items.title: Binary restricted Boltzmann machine, exact likelihood gradient, and finite contrastive divergence
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $m,n\ge1$, visible states $v\in\{0,1\}^m$, hidden states $h\in\{0,1\}^n$, biases $a\in\mathbb R^m$ and $b\in\mathbb R^n$, and weights $W\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$; a finite bipartite graph is specified by requiring $W_{ij}=0$ at every absent visible-hidden edge. Define $E(v,h)=-a^Tv-b^Th-v^TWh$, $Z=\sum_{v,h}\exp(-E(v,h))$, and $p(v,h)=Z^{-1}\exp(-E(v,h))$; $Z$ is finite and positive. Set $p(v)=\sum_h p(v,h)$, and let $V,H$ be the coordinate variables under $p$. For a finite mass function $q$, write $\mathbb E_q[g]=\sum_xq(x)g(x)$. With $\sigma(t)=(1+\exp(-t))^{-1}$, and $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(u;r)$ the mass on $\{0,1\}$ with probability $r$ at $1$, the layer conditionals factorize as
$$p(h\mid v)=\prod_{j=1}^n\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(h_j;\sigma\!\left(b_j+(W^Tv)_j\right)\right),\qquad p(v\mid h)=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(v_i;\sigma\!\left(a_i+(Wh)_i\right)\right),$$
so each layer is conditionally independent given the other. For one observed $v$, the exact gradients are
$$\frac{\partial\log p(v)}{\partial W_{ij}}=v_i\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v)}[h_j]-\mathbb E_p[V_iH_j],\qquad \frac{\partial\log p(v)}{\partial a_i}=v_i-\mathbb E_p[V_i],\qquad \frac{\partial\log p(v)}{\partial b_j}=\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v)}[h_j]-\mathbb E_p[H_j].$$
These are ambient derivatives in all parameters, evaluated at the specified $W$; when a graph fixes absent-edge weights to zero, retain only allowed-edge derivatives as free parameters. Define $K(v,v')=\sum_h p(h\mid v)p(v'\mid h)$, a row-stochastic transition matrix. Starting from $q_0^v=\delta_v$, let $q_k^v=q_0^vK^k$ for a finite integer $k\ge1$. For one observed $v$, define the finite contrastive-divergence components by
$$\widehat g^{(k)}_{W_{ij}}(v)=v_i\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v)}[h_j]-\sum_{v'}q_k^v(v')v'_i\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v')}[h_j],\quad \widehat g^{(k)}_{a_i}(v)=v_i-\sum_{v'}q_k^v(v')v'_i,\quad \widehat g^{(k)}_{b_j}(v)=\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v)}[h_j]-\sum_{v'}q_k^v(v')\mathbb E_{p(h\mid v')}[h_j].$$
They replace the exact negative-phase expectations under $p(v')$ by expectations under the finite $k$-step law $q_k^v$ and conditional hidden law $p(h\mid v')$. This finite-chain statistic is an approximation; no equality to the exact likelihood gradient or chain-convergence claim is asserted.

items.title: Gaussian precision zeros characterize pairwise conditional independence
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $p\ge2$ and let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_p)$ have multivariate normal law $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)$ with real symmetric positive-definite covariance $\Sigma$; put $\Theta=\Sigma^{-1}$. For every pair of distinct indices $i,j$, $X_i$ and $X_j$ are conditionally independent given $\sigma(X_k:k\notin\{i,j\})$ if and only if $\Theta_{ij}=0$. Thus the graph whose edges are exactly the nonzero off-diagonal entries of $\Theta$ is the Gaussian pairwise conditional-dependence graph.

items.title: The Gaussian profile likelihood reduces to the trace score
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $N,p\ge1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^p$ be independent observations with common law $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is real symmetric positive definite; put $\Theta=\Sigma^{-1}$, $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^N x_r$, and $S=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^N(x_r-\bar x)(x_r-\bar x)^T$. The log-likelihood maximized over $\mu$ is
$$-\frac{Np}{2}\log(2\pi)+\frac N2\bigl(\log\det\Theta-\operatorname{tr}(S\Theta)\bigr).$$
Thus, after removing the additive constant and multiplying by $2/N$, the normalized Gaussian profile-likelihood score is $\log\det\Theta-\operatorname{tr}(S\Theta)$.

items.title: Finite-budget block and cyclic-coordinate graphical-lasso procedure
items.statement:
Input an integer $p\ge2$, a real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix $S\in\mathbb S_+^p$, a real $\lambda>0$, and positive integers $R,K$. The output is either `failure` or a matrix $\Theta\in\mathbb S_{++}^p$. Let $I_p$ be the $p\times p$ identity, $t_+=\max(t,0)$, $\operatorname{sign}(t)=1$ for $t>0$, $0$ for $t=0$, and $-1$ for $t<0$, and $\mathsf{Soft}(t,\lambda)=\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-\lambda)_+$. Initialize $W=S+\lambda I_p$.

For each outer sweep $r=1,\ldots,R$, and within it for each original-coordinate index $j=1,\ldots,p$, use the temporary coordinate order $\pi_j=(1,\ldots,j-1,j+1,\ldots,p,j)$. Form the same reindexing of both matrices, $S^{(j)}_{ab}=S_{\pi_j(a),\pi_j(b)}$ and $W^{(j)}_{ab}=W_{\pi_j(a),\pi_j(b)}$, for $1\le a,b\le p$. Set $V=(W^{(j)}_{ab})_{a,b<p}$, $s=(S^{(j)}_{a,p})_{a<p}$, and $d=W^{(j)}_{pp}$. Initialize $\beta=0\in\mathbb R^{p-1}$. For each of $K$ inner sweeps, update coordinates $\ell=1,\ldots,p-1$ in increasing order: if $V_{\ell\ell}\le0$, return `failure`; otherwise set
$$\beta_\ell\leftarrow\frac{\mathsf{Soft}\!\left(s_\ell-\sum_{\substack{1\le k<p\\k\ne\ell}}V_{\ell k}\beta_k,\lambda\right)}{V_{\ell\ell}}.$$

After the inner sweeps, form $\widetilde W^{(j)}=\begin{pmatrix}V&V\beta\\(V\beta)^T&d\end{pmatrix}$. Restore original indexing by forming the candidate matrix $W^{\mathrm{cand}}$ with $W^{\mathrm{cand}}_{\pi_j(a),\pi_j(b)}=\widetilde W^{(j)}_{ab}$ for all $1\le a,b\le p$. Compute a symmetric eigendecomposition of $W^{\mathrm{cand}}$; if any eigenvalue is nonpositive, return `failure`. Otherwise set $W=W^{\mathrm{cand}}$ before proceeding to the next original-coordinate index $j$. After all $R$ sweeps, return $\Theta=W^{-1}$. This bounded truncation of the coupled block and lasso updates makes no convergence or optimizer claim.

items.title: Coordinate minimization, positive-definiteness invariant and termination of the finite-budget graphical-lasso procedure
items.statement:
Let $p\ge2$ be an integer, $S\in\mathbb S_+^p$ be real symmetric positive semidefinite, $\lambda>0$, and $R,K$ be positive integers. Execute the finite-budget block and cyclic-coordinate graphical-lasso procedure with these inputs in exact real arithmetic, treating its finite-dimensional matrix operations as exact operations. The initialized matrix and every accepted matrix $W$ are symmetric positive definite. In every block reached before failure, its principal matrix $V$ is positive definite, every $V_{\ell\ell}>0$, and every coordinate update is well-defined and uniquely minimizes
$$Q_{V,s}(\beta)=\tfrac12\beta^TV\beta-s^T\beta+\lambda\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}|\beta_k|$$
with all other coordinates fixed. Each candidate matrix is finite and symmetric; it is accepted exactly when positive definite. The procedure terminates after at most $RpK(p-1)$ coordinate updates and $Rp$ candidate eigenvalue tests, returning either `failure` or a symmetric positive-definite matrix $\Theta=W^{-1}$. These assertions do not assert convergence of the iterates or global optimality for the sparse-precision objective.

items.title: The all-entry graphical-lasso objective has a unique KKT optimizer
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb S_+^p$ be the real symmetric positive-semidefinite $p\times p$ matrices and $\mathbb S_{++}^p$ the real symmetric positive-definite ones. For $p\ge1$, $S\in\mathbb S_+^p$ and $\lambda>0$, maximize
$$F_{S,\lambda}(\Theta)=\log\det\Theta-\operatorname{tr}(S\Theta)-\lambda\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^p|\Theta_{ij}|$$
over $\Theta\in\mathbb S_{++}^p$. The objective is strictly concave and attains a unique maximizer $\Theta^*$. A feasible $\Theta$ is this unique maximizer if and only if there is a symmetric matrix $\Gamma$ such that $\Theta^{-1}-S-\lambda\Gamma=0$, with $\Gamma_{ii}=1$, $\Gamma_{ij}=\operatorname{sign}(\Theta_{ij})$ when $\Theta_{ij}\ne0$, and $\Gamma_{ij}\in[-1,1]$ when $\Theta_{ij}=0$.

title: Undirected graphical models and sparse precision estimation — Examples

items.title: Visible RBM units are conditionally independent but dependent marginally
items.statement: Assume AC. In a binary restricted Boltzmann machine with two visible units, one hidden unit, $a=(0,0)$, $b=0$ and $W_{11}=W_{21}=\log3$, the visible units are independent conditional on the hidden unit. Each conditional success probability is $1/2$ when $H=0$ and $3/4$ when $H=1$. Marginally, $P(V_1=1)=P(V_2=1)=7/10$ and $P(V_1=1,V_2=1)=1/2\ne49/100$, so $V_1$ and $V_2$ are dependent.

items.title: A three-node Gaussian chain has conditionally independent endpoints
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\Theta=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}$, $\Sigma=\Theta^{-1}$, and $X\sim N_3(0,\Sigma)$. Put an edge between $i$ and $j$ exactly when $\Theta_{ij}\ne0$. Then the graph is the path $1-2-3$, and $X_1$ and $X_3$ are conditionally independent given $X_2$.

items.title: Increasing λ creates an exact zero edge in a two-variable graphical lasso
items.statement: Take observations $x_1=(1,1)^T$ and $x_2=(-1,-1)^T$, so their centered sample covariance is $S=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$. Under the all-entry penalty objective, every $\lambda\ge1$ gives the unique maximizer $\Theta=(1+\lambda)^{-1}I_2$ with $\Theta_{12}=0$, while for $0<\lambda<1$ every optimizer has $\Theta_{12}\ne0$. In particular, $\lambda=2$ yields a zero edge and $\lambda=\tfrac12$ yields a nonzero edge.
